title: Relationship Between Sales, Sex, and Indigenous Self-Identification for Entrepreneurs in Mexico from 2016 to 2022
content: The objective of this research is to estimate the differences in sales levels between businesses operated by individuals who self-identify as indigenous (IE) and those who do not (NIE), as well as between men (ME) and women (WE), and how this intersection may affect their sales levels. To achieve this, an Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) will be employed to compare the means between the analyzed groups, and Tukey's Honestly Significant Differences (HSD) will be used to determine the magnitude and direction of these differences. The study results reveal that businesses led by indigenous individuals have sales that are 26% below the general average, while businesses led by women show a 70.6% reduction in the same comparison. Furthermore, businesses led by indigenous women have, on average, 93.5% lower sales. These findings suggest that the challenges faced by entrepreneurs reflect the structural inequalities observed in other areas of society, highlighting the need for public and private actions focused on reducing these gaps.
